June 2010 ## A whole new world - Our revised data confirms that global consumption of copper and copper alloy mill products recovered by 26.1% y-o-y in Q1 2010. The improvements in copper and copper alloy flat rolled product markets are sound, with Asia and the Americas leading the y-o-y growth of 30-40% in the first quarter. Participants in the alloy rod market are feeling more optimistic for Q2 and Q3. Copper tube remained the weakest link as world consumption only edged up by 4.4% y-o-y, dragged down by negative growth in the Americas. - While most of the copper and copper alloy semis markets are out of the recession, a new world with new rules has emerged. Due to the impact of the global crisis and high metal prices, Wieland, one of the world’s leading fabricators, announced that the company will reduce the payment terms for deliveries by one third, effective from 1st May 2010. We believe that it is likely that other producers will follow suit. |Consumptio

On a sequential basis, the figure was up by 11%. European output was up only slightly to 107,000t, mainly supported by increases in Germany, France and Eastern and Central Europe. German production rose by 10% y-o-y to 45,000t in Q1. North East Asian copper PSSF output rebounded by 72% y-o-y to 154,000t in Q1. China, world’s largest national producer, saw a 72% y-o-y increase to 165,000t. World output of alloy PSSF recovered by 39% y-o-y to 512,000t in Q1. That was also 9% sequential growth. US output experienced robust y-o-y and sequential rebound to 67,000t. German output soared by 41% y-o-y to 42,000t but was down by 8% from the previous quarter. North East Asian output more than doubled to 97,000t compared to year-ago levels. Chinese output was 165,000t, up by 14% y-o-y and 7% q-o-q. ### Trade World copper PSSF trade recovered by 55% to 249,000t in Q1. Our numbers show that German exports amounted to 33,500t in Q1, a 7% y-o-y increase. Japanese exports soared to 20,600t, up from 6,500 a year ago. The figure for South Korea almost doubled to 15,800t whilst Taiwanese exports rose by 59% y- o-y to 45,200t. Chinese imports of copper PSSF saw a 76% y-o-y growth to 122,000t in the same period. South Korean imports reached 13,800t, up by 51%. World alloy PSSF trade amounted to 169,000t in Q1, almost double compared to year-ago levels. German exports increased to 38,900t from 20,800t. Japanese exports saw robust y-o-y recovery to 20,300t from 5,600t. South Korean exports were 14,600t whilst Taiwanese exports were 13,900t. Chinese imports of alloy PSSF more than doubled to 53,000t; but this is well below earlier years, mainly attributed to ongoing massive capacity installed in China. ### Tales from selected rolled copper product markets The rolled copper product segment in Western Europe has seen a remarkable recovery since the beginning of the year. This upturn is significantly attributed to the rebound in the German industrial activity. From an end-use perspective, European demand related to industrial applications is recovering; however, demand connected to the construction industry remains sluggish. On the other hand, the Chinese construction sector continues to be subsidised by the government, as does the domestic electrical appliance sector. As a result, Chinese fabricators’ order books, especially for sheet and strip products, were full in Q1. That was mainly driven by the rebound in the exports of end-users. Japan has also seen strong recovery in the automotive and electronics industries that use connectors and semiconductors. On anticipation of increasing demand, **Hi

tachi Cable** will raise its strip output by 19% to 3,500t in H1 and 7% to 3,700t in H2. A growing end-use market is automotive lithium-ion batteries. With that prospect, **Furukawa Electric** is planning to boost capacity of its NC-WS foil to 7.5 million square metres per month in FY2011 from 5.5 million in FY2010. Taiwan is expected to exhibit robust recovery in 2010, particularly in its foil business whilst South Korea is expanding its sheet and strip capacity, supported by strong Chinese demand. Optimistic anticipations for Taiwan are also generated by the Free Trade Agreement with the Mainland. ### Special focus: Brazil During CRU’s recent trip to Brazil, we were told that, according to **Sindicel** and **ABC,** rolled products domestic output fell by 18% to 33,000t in 2009. Brazilian fabricators’ sales strategies are focused more on the domestic business, which was considerably less affected by the global economic crisis. CRU understood that the local market is strong and Brazilian fabricators have full order books until the end of summer and are currently operating at full capacity. An end-use market with significant contribution is the automotive sector. According to ABC, 17 automakers in Brazil produced 3.2 million vehicles in 2009, with the prospect of reaching 3.5 million vehicles in 2010. © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 12 **June 2010** Copper and copper alloy mill products **www.crumonitor.com** |Copper pla|te, s|heet|, stri|p and|foil|||||||||| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |**('000 tonnes)**|||**2008**|||**% Ch**|||**2009**|||**% Ch**|**2010**|**% Ch**| ||**Q1**|**Q2**|**Q3**

Based on our revised analysis of global market trends in Q1 2010, we now estimate that world copper tube consumption rose by only 4.4% y-o-y to 548,000t from 525,000t a year ago.  Although this does represent a stronger sequential gain of 8.3% from 506,000t in Q4 2009, it is still clear that the copper tube business has benefitted least from the gradual improvement in the world economy.  This should not be so surprising in a market that is effectively dominated by the fortunes of the ailing construction and heating ventilation air conditioning and refrigeration end use sectors that are tied directly or indirectly to building activity levels in residential and non-residential markets.  Moreover, it is also this segment where copper price issues are sensitive to restocking / destocking movements and substitution / economization trends. 

### US mills gaining from preliminary anti-dumping duties 

The announcement of preliminary anti-dumping duties of 10.26% for imports from the **Golden Dragon Group** and 58.69% from the **Hailiang Group** , five other Chinese exports at 34.48% and all others at 60.50%, coupled with anti-dumping duties on Mexican imports from **IUSA** at 29.52% and **Nacobre** at 32.27% and all others (Golden Dragon and **Luvata** ) at 30.90% has already had a noticeable impact US copper tube orders (mainly from May onwards) as importers switch back to local US mills.  Mexican and Chinese exporters have requested that the final determination will be delayed by up to four and a half months to give them time to prepare evidence to challenge or mitigate the level or extent of future antidumping duties.  If the preliminary anti-dumping duties were enforced at the current level then Golden Dragon’s new Mexican mill would stand to face anti-dumping duties of 30.90% compared to 10.26% for Golden Dragon’s exports from China – a severe competitive disadvantage considering the investment outlay on brand new equipment and facilities.  Luvata would also stand to be similarly hit.  There have already been two follow-on developments to this news.  Firstly **Wieland** will acquire the 40% stake of **KobeWieland Copper Products** that **Kobelco** owns as of October 1<sup>st</sup> 2010, whereupon it will be renamed **Wieland Copper Products LLC** .  And secondly, Hailiang has inferred that it will consider moving the manufacturing of its US tube export business from China to its new 71,000tpy capacity copper and alloy tube facility in Vietnam which it is now commissioning.  The trial continues… 

### China strengthening on domestic appliance sales 

Domestic demand for commercial tube has benefitted from a strong surge in home appliance production in the opening four months of 2010.  Air conditioner output jumped 30% y-o-y to 36M units; refrigerator shipments leapt 29% y-o-y to 24M units while washing machine assembly climbed 40% y-o-y to 19M units.  Although the y-o-y rate of growth is predicted to decelerate as

the year progresses it is still expected that the output of the above items will grow by between 11-15%. Local analysts attribute the good growth to the government’s “home appliances to the countryside” and “new for old” replacement programs designed to stimulate sales growth with a variety of discounts and trade in benefits. Export demand for copper tube, air conditioners and other appliances has yet to see any significant improvement, so copper tubemaker’s fortunes are largely being dictated by the speed of the domestic sales recovery. ### Brighter outlook for the remainder of Asia The prospects in Asia outside China are starting to look a bit brighter. Japanese copper tube output rose 16% y-o-y in the first four months of the year and South Korean production increased by 8% y-o-y. We also hear more encouraging reports of higher production levels through Malaysia and Thailand. But the consequences of the earlier and faster recovery in Developing Asia, driven by customer migration are inevitable. **Furukawa Electric** has said it will review the status of its Japanese tube mill in Amagasaki, by end-2011. The likely outcome is that production will cease and orders will be transferred to its subsidiaries in China and Thailand, which are closer to the customer base and are more cost competitive. 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 6 of 12 www.crumonitor.com **June 2010** Copper and copper alloy mill products |Copper tub|e|||||||||||||| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |**('000 tonnes)**|||**2008**|||**% Ch**|||**2009**|||**% Ch**|**2010**|**% Ch**| ||**Q1**|**Q2**|**Q3**

We believe that North East Asia contributed most of this growth, with its output rising by 52.0% y-o-y and 3.6% q-o-q to 125,000t in Q1 2010. We also estimate that demand in the Western World has improved, supported by the automotive and appliance sectors, with output in Americas growing by 15.6% y-o-y to 80,000t and European production growing by 25.4% y-o-y to 279,000t in Q1 2010. ### Restocking and product development in North East Asia The latest trade data confirmed that Asia was leading the growth in global brass rod markets, with total output surging 35.5% y-o-y to 382,000t in Q1 2010. Much of this growth was attributed to North East Asia. Taiwanese and South Korean output increased by 72.7% y-o-y and 22.5% y-o-y, respectively, in the first quarter of this year. Japanese production was up significantly by 83.0% y-o-y to 52,000t, almost matching the pre-crisis level in Q3 2008. **San-Etsu Metals** , a major Japanese producer, plans to market a new lead-free brass alloy, which contains carbon as lubricant agent alternate for lead within FY2012 ending March 2013. It is reported that the company will carry out test production of large size extruded alloy bullets and evaluation of secondary processing for sinter forging alloy products in FY2010. This type of alloy is suitable for manufacturing electronic and optical components. ### European mills confident for the short term Compared to our estimates in April, we have now revised up Western European production by 37,000t to 223,000t based on recent conversations with local fabricators. Most market participants are feeling optimistic as they have seen promising signs throughout Q2 showing that business is coming back. The German brass rod market exhibited a 40.8% increase q-o-q in Q1 2010, underpinned by sound improvements in industrial and automotive production. A German producer said during a phone interview that the company is doing much better in Q2 compared to last year and production volumes are up 20% y-o-y. The European market in general is doing well,

apart from Spain, which is still troubled by the depressed construction sector. Customers remain cautious as orders are very short term, around 3 to 4 weeks ahead, while for the same volumes people would normally book 2 to 3 months in advance before the crisis. Italian producer **KME** reported in mid-May that its rods segment saw strong sales recovery in Q1 2010. It was reported on Reuters that Werner Riegert, Head of Procurement of **Swissmetal** , said that he expects to use 30% more copper this year given that demand has strengthened since Q3 2009. Order entries for Q1 2010 have increased by 44% on Q4 2009. However, fabricators are worried about Q4 2010 and next year, particularly for demand from the auto sector as by then all the scrappage premium will end. ### North American market improved but lagging behind others US alloy rod imports grew by 11.3% to 6,588t while exports rose by 15.7% to 4,670t in Q1 2010. We believe this is mainly due to restocking activities in the domestic market and also export demand to the Canadian market, which saw imports climbing 20.2% q-o-q, and some parts of South and Central America, where consumption increased from 58,000t in Q4 2009 to 59,000t in Q1 2010. We now estimate that US brass rod output increased sequentially from 51,000t in Q4 2009 to 57,000t in Q1 2010 while South and Central American output in Q1 was down on Q4 but up 12.0% y-o-y. **Mueller Industries** reported brass fittings and OEM volumes improved during Q1 2010 due to better demand. We hear that the general consensus is the North American market is going to continue improving but there will not be dramatic sequential gains for the rest of this year as commercial construction remains sluggish. 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 8 of 12 **June 2010** Copper and copper alloy mill products www.crumonitor.com |Copper allo|y ro|ds, b|ars a|nd s|ectio|ns||||||||| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |**('000 tonnes)**|||**2008**|||**% Ch**|||**2009**|||**% Ch**|**2010**|**% Ch**| ||**Q1**|**Q2**|**Q3**|**Q4**|**Year**|**07-08**|**Q1**|**Q2**|**Q3**|**Q4**|**Year**|**08-09**|**Q1**|**09-10**| |**_Production_**||||||||||||||| |Canada|0|0|0|0|**0**|na|0|0|0|0|**0**|na|0|na| |United States

Data: LME Since mid-April, copper prices have been on a downward trajectory, driven by downbeat macroeconomic news, rather than developments in the copper market. Copper demand has actually picked up seasonally, with exchange stocks declining by a daily average of over 2,600t/d since the beginning of May. However, despite this fundamental support, copper prices fell along with other LME metals when renewed fears over the Greek debt crisis saw a strengthening in the US dollar in the second half of the month. In May copper prices remained volatile driven by swings in sentiment about the macro economy. Having started the month at over $7,000/t, copper prices fell to below $6,500/t on 19th May only to recover to over $6,900/t by the end of May. In early June, renewed fears over the impact of the debt crisis pushed the euro down to a new fouryear low of just under $1.19/€. The resulting contagion spread to copper prices, which fell to almost $6,100/t on 7th June. #### **Zinc** Zinc price movements largely mirrored those of copper in the second half of April. Since the beginning of May, though, it has suffered larger percentage declines. Penalty margins range from 10.26-60.50% for China, and 29.5232.27% for Mexico. Some 9 Chinese exporters qualified for a separate dumping rate from 10.2634.48%; all others will be charged at the 60.50% rate. In 2009, these imports were valued at US$233.0m (China) and US$130.3m (Mexico). Subsequently, on 9 June China’s **Golden Dragon Copper Rod Group** reported one of the largest American air conditioner producers had said it would pay the antidumping duty guarantee money on its copper pipe purchases for GD Copper. - US exports of brass mill products in March surged 26.1% y/y to 21.8m lbs (after February’s 1.6% drop), while imports increased 7.5% to 41.9m lbs, according to data from the **Copper and Brass Fabricators Council** . Canada was the leading export destination (8.2m lbs) while Mexico supplied the most imports (9.6m lbs). Imports/exports breakdown was: sheet, strip, plate and foil products 12.0m lbs/ 9.0m lbs; pipe and tube products 16.9m lbs/ 5.5m lbs; profiles, rods and bars 10.0m lbs/ 4.3m lbs; copper alloy wire 3.0m lbs/ 3.0m lbs. ### Europe - **Luvata** ’s VP of sales, marketing and product development at the tubes division reports mixed demand outlook but says the air conditioning industry as a whole should see strong sustained growth rates of 3-6% this year. In Europe, demand for copper tubing for air conditioners has been weaker than the generally flat expectations for that market. The North American market has delivered 10% growth in residential sales but a flat performance in the commercial sector, which is expected to continue steady into next year. The Asian market's performance has been quite strong and robust, within the 3-6% growth expectation so far this year, and continued growth is expected. - **Boliden** lost its appeal to cut the size of a €32.6m (US$40m) fine which was imposed on the Swedish mining and smelting company (and its two former subsidiaries Boliden Cuivre et Zinc (BCZ) and Boliden Fabrication) in September 2004, by the EU Commission. The company was fined for engaging in activities designed to restrict competition in the European market for sanitary copper tubing. - **KME Group** reports that its Q1 output of semi-finished copper, copper alloy and special products rose 10.5% y/y to 126kt, and says the full-year output should be up 1

0-12%. Demand picked up from the auto and domestic appliance sectors, especially in Germany, and from manufacturers of components for renewable energy generation, but construction remains weak. The rods segment saw strong sales recovery. 

### North East Asia 

- **Furukawa Electric Co. Ltd** . has announced a review of its copper tube business in response to a shrinking domestic market and in a bid to return the business to profitability. The Japanese firm aims to make final decisions by 2011 on restructuring to improve productivity and specialise in high-grade products, possibly pulling out of low-value added products including water pipe. 

- Japan’s output of copper and copper-alloy fabricated products, including sheets and tubes, jumped 67% y/y in April to 74,100 tonnes, as demand recovers with economic growth in China and other Asian nations, according to preliminary data from the **Japan Copper and Brass Association** . This is the sixth straight month of y/y increases but April’s figure is 2.4% down on 75,894 tonnes reported in March, when output more than doubled y/y. 

- **Poongsan Corp** . has raised its sales targets, backed by strong Chinese demand, and expects to sell some 210,000t of copper and alloy semis this year, compared to an earlier forecast of 205,000t.  In addition, the South Korean company is expanding capacity in sheet and strip products used in electronics. It plans to increase sheet and strip capacity by 22% by 2012.

### Developing Asia 

- **Hailiang Co. Ltd** ., China’s second largest copper tube manufacturer, said it will move its US copper tube orders to its Vietnamese subsidiary to avoid the 58.69% duty imposed on its products by the US Commerce Dept’s preliminary anti-dumping ruling of 6 May. The recently completed 71ktpy capacity Vietnamese operation is now in trial production. In 2009, Hailiang exported 10,701t copper tube to the US (7.18% of total sales). 

- **Golden Dragon Copper Group** has kicked off its 200m yuan (US$29.3m) copper tube production line project in Handan City, Hebei. The project has the capacity to produce 2.5mtpy sets of air conditioner pipe fittings and 1.5mtpy sets of refrigerator pipe fittings. The group has a current yearly production capacity of 220kt, including 150kt grooved tubes. 

- At **Antaike's 5th China Copper Processing Industry Development Forum** (held on May 19), **Mr. Li Huchun** , a senior engineer from one of China’s large-scale air conditioner producers, predicted that copper consumption in the air conditioner industry would increase between 8-12%. He said output of China’s seven leading air conditioner producers would be 58.5m units in 2010, and copper tube demand would be 333.6kt. 

- **Chinese customs office** data shows that China’s imports of unwrought copper and copper products in April rose 9.1% y/y to 436,345 tonnes, b
